question: Should transient tool-progress intent become a supported typed cross-plugin reply contract, or should Slack suppression remain entirely within the existing shared progress-draft pipeline?
rationale: The branch avoids public SDK growth by using private metadata, but that leaves Codex and Slack coupled through an undocumented literal; automation cannot choose the permanent product and ownership boundary.

options.title: Use a typed shared contract
options.body: Add a narrow progress-intent type at the shared reply/progress boundary, document its lifecycle, and migrate Codex and Slack together.

options.title: Use the progress-draft pipeline
options.body: Remove the Codex-to-Slack marker and repair the established shared progress path so channels do not interpret producer-specific metadata.

options.title: Accept the private convention
options.body: Land the duplicated private literal and explicitly own its compatibility and maintenance risk.

recommendation.title: Use a typed shared contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow progress-intent type at the shared reply/progress boundary, document its lifecycle, and migrate Codex and Slack together.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared progress-draft and channel-delivery work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the permanent owner-boundary choice.
